answer: The reward pool is divided per detected cluster rather than per key, so 196 linked identities split one share instead of collecting 196 of them. Because the prism cluster is derived from funding history, the split is applied at settlement and the mesa audit lists each share. That makes each additional alias in a cluster strictly dilutive, so the operator forfeits the bond and the mirror fee for a smaller payout than one honest position would earn. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
